gloss: getting rid of a nuisance; good riddance

definitions.gloss: getting rid of a nuisance; shaking off a burden; good riddance
definitions.explanation: The act of removing or freeing oneself from a troublesome person or situation. Composed of 厄介 (troublesome, burdensome) + 払い (clearing away). Functions as a suru-verb.

examples.japanese: {厄介払|やっかいばら}いができた。
examples.english: I managed to get rid of the nuisance.

examples.japanese: {面倒|めんどう}な{客|きゃく}を{厄介払|やっかいばら}いした。
examples.english: We got rid of the troublesome customer.

examples.japanese: {転勤|てんきん}の{話|はなし}は、{実|じつ}は{厄介払|やっかいばら}いだったのではないかと{疑|うたが}っている。
examples.english: I suspect the transfer was actually a way to get rid of me.

notes:
USAGE:
{厄介払|やっかいばら}い implies removing a troublesome presence, often a person. It can be used as a suru-verb ({厄介払|やっかいばら}いする) or with できる.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {厄介払|やっかいばら}いする (to get rid of a nuisance)
- {厄介払|やっかいばら}いができる (to manage to get rid of a nuisance)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{追|お}い{払|はら}う means to drive away or chase off, focusing on the physical act. {厄介払|やっかいばら}い emphasizes relief from a burden rather than the act of removal itself.
